# `provider_availability_notify`

**Announce a provider's availability change.** Message the global supervisor and the human once when a provider moves between launchable and unavailable; a repeat for the same change sends nothing.

|---|---|
| Capability | `provider_availability_notify` |
| Side effect | `create` |
| Idempotency | natural |
| Retry safe | yes |
| Timeout | none |
| Preview | not supported |

## Purpose

Tell the people who can act that a provider -- a harness login such as
`codex` or `claude` -- has crossed between *launchable* and *unavailable*.
When Codex's login disappears, the global supervisor and the human operator
should each get exactly one message saying what state it is in, why, since
when, when it is expected back, what to run to fix it and how much queued work
it is holding. The command sends that message once per change of state, however
many times it is asked
([provider failover](../../specs/provider-failover.md) D19).

## When a playbook uses it

The daemon calls it itself on every change of half, so an install with no
playbook still hears about an outage. It is contracted so the
`provider-failover` system playbook can call it on `provider.state_changed`
and on its periodic timer as a backstop: a notice the daemon already sent comes
back `already_notified`, never a second message. It is excluded from MCP, the
CLI and the typed API; operators read state with `aq provider status`.

## How it works internally

1. [`ProviderCommandsMixin._cmd_provider_availability_notify`](../../../src/commands/provider_commands.py)
   resolves the provider (a vendor alias such as `openai` names `codex`) and
   hands it to the availability service.
2. [`ProviderAvailabilityService.notify_state_change`](../../../src/providers/availability_service.py)
   reads the transitions of the last `recovery.flap_window_seconds`. A
   generation whose transition stayed in one half is `not_a_half_change`.
3. More than `notify.flap_threshold` half changes in the window send one
   *flapping* notice and then damp further ones (`flap_damped`) until the
   provider holds one half for a full window.
4. `claim_provider_notification` compare-and-swaps
   `provider_availability.notified_generation`; only the caller that moves it
   sends, everyone else gets `already_notified`.
5. The message -- state, reason, since, expected recovery, remediation, held
   task count, affected role profiles and the exact `aq provider` commands --
   is queued to `session:supervisor-global` and `user:dashboard` from
   `system/playbook:provider-failover`.

## Side effects and persistence

Two rows in `messages` (one per recipient) and the `notified_generation`
column of the provider's `provider_availability` row. Both are durable, so a
restart never re-sends a notice for a generation already announced. The
flapping notice's timestamp is held in memory and resets on restart.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

| Outcome | Cause | Diagnose with |
|---|---|---|
| `rejected` | Unknown provider, or availability tracking is not running. | `aq provider status` lists the tracked providers. |
| `messages_disabled` | `messages.enabled` is false; nothing can be queued. | `aq system config get messages` |
| `disabled` | `provider_failover.notify.supervisor` is false. | `aq system config get provider_failover` |
| `flap_damped` | The provider is flapping; one notice was already sent this window. | `aq provider history --provider <provider>` |

  "save_result_as": "notice",

    "notified": "announce-provider-state--done",
    "flapping": "announce-provider-state--done",
    "already_notified": "announce-provider-state--done",
    "flap_damped": "announce-provider-state--done",
    "not_a_half_change": "announce-provider-state--done",
    "disabled": "announce-provider-state--done",
    "messages_disabled": "announce-provider-state--done",
    "rejected": "announce-provider-state--failed",
    "runtime_error": "announce-provider-state--failed"
  }
}
